default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-039.title: Fair-value-gap retest hold
E-039.hypothesis: A three-bar gap (bar low above the high two bars earlier) marks a burst of one-sided market orders that left no two-sided trade in the zone; when price first comes back into the zone and closes back out on the impulse side, the impulse side's remaining resting orders absorbed the late counter-traders; follow it.

E-040.title: Clock-hour open defence
E-040.hypothesis: Hourly candles are the frame many desks and chart traders read; after the hour ran well away from its open, a return to the hour's open that closes back on the excursion side shows the side ahead for the hour defending a green (red) candle, and the retest-sellers are trapped; trade back toward the excursion.

E-041.title: Pre-flatten day-move fade
E-041.hypothesis: In the last hour or two the day traders who rode the day's move (and retail accounts facing broker auto-flatten) must close, which is order flow against the day's direction; on a day already moved more than usual for the minute, a bar closing beyond the previous bar against the move starts that unwind; fade.

E-042.title: Weak-volume new-extreme push fade
E-042.hypothesis: A new recent high made on clearly less volume than the previous push to a high, and closing in the lower half of its bar, means fewer aggressive buyers answer each new price while sellers stay; the push is the last buyers' exhaustion, so fade it (mirror for lows).

E-043.title: Accelerating-burst exhaustion fade
E-043.hypothesis: Consecutive same-direction bars with each range larger than the last, ending in an unusually large bar, are a stop/momentum-ignition cascade; once the next bar fails to extend and closes against it, the forced orders are spent and liquidity providers pull price back; fade.

E-044.title: Failed strong-close bar fade
E-044.hypothesis: A large bar that closes at its extreme attracts chasers at the close; when the very next bar closes back beyond that bar's midpoint, the chasers are under water at once and their stops sit just behind, so their exits push the reversal; fade the strong bar.

E-045.title: Wick-imbalance range break
E-045.hypothesis: When the recent bars carry much longer lower wicks than upper wicks, dips keep being bought by passive buyers while offers are lifted without rejection; a close through the window's high then confirms the absorbing side has won; follow the break in the direction of the wick imbalance.

E-046.title: ADR-fraction level fade from the open
E-046.hypothesis: Day traders set targets as fractions of the average daily range measured from the session open; at each open +/- j x frac x ADR take-profit orders rest, so a bar that reaches such a level from the open side and closes back shows the targets absorbing the push; fade back toward the open.

E-047.title: Three-push wedge fade
E-047.hypothesis: Three separate pushes to new short-term highs inside one window (a wedge) show each leg being sold into again; when the bar after the third push closes below the prior bar's low, the late buyers of the third push are trapped and the move reverts; fade (mirror for lows).

E-048.title: Prior-session closing VWAP rejection
E-048.hypothesis: The volume-weighted price of yesterday's closing window is where index funds and institutions executed their close-benchmarked orders; they defend or re-enter near it, so a bar that reaches it from one side and closes back on that side meets their resting orders; trade away from the level.
